This repository already contains `logredact`, a command-line tool that removes personal data from log files. Read the existing code and any documentation in the repository before changing it. Change it as follows; everything else it does now must keep working exactly as it does.

1. **Phone numbers.** Phone numbers in international format, a `+` followed by 8 to 15 digits such as `+14155552671`, become `[PHONE]`. With `--count`, the summary on standard error becomes `emails=N ips=N cards=N phones=N`.

2. **Output folder.** A new option `--out-dir DIR` writes the redacted lines of each FILE to a file with the same name in DIR (the file's name only, without its directories) instead of to standard output. DIR is created, with any missing parent directories, if it does not exist, and an existing file of that name in DIR is replaced. When every FILE has been processed, the tool prints `wrote N files` to standard output, where N is the number of output files written. A FILE that cannot be read is handled as it is now: an error message naming the file on standard error, and exit status 2.

Examples, for files `app.log` (containing `user jane@example.com`) and `web.log` (containing `GET / from 10.0.0.7`):

```
$ printf 'call +14155552671 now\n' | python -m logredact
call [PHONE] now

$ printf 'a@b.io +442071838750\n' | python -m logredact --count
[EMAIL] [PHONE]
emails=1 ips=0 cards=0 phones=1        <- on standard error

$ python -m logredact --out-dir clean app.log web.log
wrote 2 files
```

Done. All 68 tests pass (66 existing + the ones I added), and every documented example from the spec reproduces exactly.

## What changed

**`src/logredact/redact.py`** — added a phone rule:
- `_PHONE = \+[0-9]{8,15}(?![0-9])(?!\.[0-9])`, placed in the alternation after `email`/`ip` but before `card`, so a `+`-prefixed number is read as a phone before its digits can be claimed as a card.
- `Counts` gained a `phones` field; `summary()` now renders `emails=N ips=N cards=N phones=N`.
- New `PHONE_TOKEN` export (also re-exported from `__init__.py`).

**`src/logredact/cli.py`** — added `--out-dir DIR`. The old stdout path is unchanged (just moved into `_to_stdout`); `_to_dir` creates `DIR` with `os.makedirs(..., exist_ok=True)`, writes each FILE to `DIR/<basename>` opened `"w"` (so an existing file is replaced), using the same `utf-8`/`surrogateescape`/`newline=''` settings so bytes still round-trip. It prints `wrote N files` after all FILEs are processed. A FILE that can't be read still names the file on stderr and exits 2, stopping the run.

**Tests and README** updated: the five existing assertions on the `--count` line now expect `phones=N` (the only pre-existing tests the change breaks — all other behaviour is untouched), plus new `PhoneTests` and `OutDirTests` classes.

## Two judgment calls worth your eye

Both are documented in the README's "Behaviour worth knowing":

1. **`--out-dir` with stdin is a usage error** (exit 2, `DIR` not created). With no FILE, or with `-`, there's no file name to reuse inside `DIR`. The alternative would have been silently falling back to stdout for those operands.

2. **`wrote N files` counts distinct output paths.** Two inputs with the same base name (`one/a.log two/a.log`) write to one path — the second replacing the first — so `N` is 1, not 2.

Also, a 13-to-15-digit Luhn-valid run preceded by `+` now redacts as `[PHONE]` rather than `[CARD]` (`+4222222222222`). That's an unavoidable overlap between the two rules; past 15 digits the phone rule doesn't apply, so `+4111111111111111` → `+[CARD]` exactly as before. I also kept the existing house rule that digits in a dotted number are left alone, so `+12345678.90` isn't treated as a phone — tell me if you'd rather have the stricter literal reading there.

I haven't committed anything.
